<details><summary>About this simulation</summary>

Practice with two synthetic files in your browser. Each mission has its own repository for the current visit. Reloading the page starts a new visit. The model supports up to five local branches and 50 commits and shows just the setting changed in each diff. For a real repository, open [the local Git lab](git-lab.qmd).

</details>

## Worked routes

<details><summary>Stage selectively</summary>

Save the rule at 0.50 s and the plot color as purple. Stage `config/analysis.toml` and compare both diffs. Commit the rule with a message explaining the change. The plot stays under Unstaged. Try editing the rule again after staging it and check the two columns of `git status -sb`.

</details>

<details><summary>Merge independent work</summary>

Create and switch to `criteria` at `c0`. Save, stage, and commit a 0.30 s minimum RT. Switch to `main`, then save, stage, and commit the purple plot. Look for `c0` in the graph and merge `criteria` into `main`. The merge commit has two parents.

</details>

<details><summary>Resolve a conflict</summary>

The mission starts with `criteria` at 0.30 s and `main` at 0.25 s. Find their shared ancestor `c0` and merge `criteria` into `main`. Compare both values, save the intended resolution, stage `config/analysis.toml`, and commit. Staging is required even if you keep the 0.25 s value already on `main`.

</details>

<details><summary>Share and review</summary>

You start on `criteria` with a local commit. Run `git push -u origin criteria`, then open the pull request. Read the proposed changes, record your review, and merge on the server. Compare local and server `main`, switch to local `main`, and run `git pull --ff-only`. To see when a review goes stale, add a labmate commit on the server after you record your review.

</details>

<details><summary>Recover a change</summary>

Save a new minimum RT and stage it. Run `git restore --staged config/analysis.toml`. Inspect the unstaged edit, then stage it again and commit. Run `git revert HEAD` and find both commits in Branches.

</details>

## Command reference

| Command | What it does here |
| --- | --- |
| `git status` / `git status -sb` | Shows staged, unstaged, and unmerged files. |
| `git diff -- PATH` / `git diff --staged -- PATH` | Shows unstaged or staged changes. Omit the path for all changed files. `--cached` also means staged. |
| `git add PATH` / `git add .` | Stages the saved working versions. |
| `git commit -m "Message"` | Records the staging area as a commit. |
| `git branch` / `git switch -c criteria` / `git switch main` | Lists branches, creates and switches, or switches to an existing branch. |
| `git merge criteria` / `git merge --abort` | Merges into the current branch or cancels an unresolved merge. |
| `git log --oneline --graph --all` | Lists locally known commits and their parents. |
| `git push -u origin criteria` | Pushes a branch and sets its upstream. After that, `git push` uses the upstream. |
| `git fetch origin` / `git pull --ff-only` | Updates remote-tracking references. Pull also advances the current branch when it can fast-forward. |
| `git restore --staged PATH` / `git restore PATH` | Unstages an edit or discards the unstaged edit. |
| `git revert HEAD` | Adds a commit that reverses the latest single-parent commit. |
